current-block: Testing if access token was revoked after authorization code reuse (the AS 'should' have revoked the access token)
comment: This AS issues stateless, self-contained JWT access tokens verified by signature/exp alone (see resource/verify.go) - there is no revocation list a resource endpoint could consult. Detecting authorization-code reuse and additionally revoking the access token it already issued is a SHOULD (RFC 6749 4.1.2), not a MUST, and the suite's own module text confirms failing to do it will not block certification. See go-fapi's conversation history / ARCHITECTURE.md for the tradeoff (stateless verification vs. a shared revocation store).

current-block: Second client: Check for refresh token
comment: The plan config's second client deliberately omits offline_access from its scope (only client 1 requests it), so no refresh token is issued for it - the suite's own message confirms this is acceptable server policy, not a defect. Client 1's own refresh flow runs and succeeds; per FAPI2-SP-FINAL 5.3.2.1-9 this AS does not rotate refresh tokens, so the suite's own module logic (FAPI2SPFinalRefreshToken.java) logs 'Refresh token not rotated. Skipping lost refresh token test.' for client 1 and cleanly continues - see the accompanying expected-skips-message-signing.json entry for why the module's overall result is still SKIPPED rather than PASSED.
